tools.name: set_project
tools.description: Select the RPG Maker MV project folder to work on (the folder containing Game.rpgproject and data/). Must be called before other tools unless the server was started with --project. Discards any open changeset (its staged edits are lost).

path.description: Absolute path to the RPG Maker MV project folder

tools.name: get_project_info
tools.description: Summary of the current project: game title, database record counts, map count, and plugin count.

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: List all records of a database type as {id, name} summaries. Use get_record for full data.

type.description: Which database to access (e.g. actors, items, skills, troops, commonEvents)

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: Get the full JSON of one database record by id.

type.description: Which database to access (e.g. actors, items, skills, troops, commonEvents)

tools.name: update_record
tools.description: Update a database record. By default the given fields are shallow-merged into the existing record; set merge=false to replace it entirely. The record's id always stays fixed to match its array position.

type.description: Which database to access (e.g. actors, items, skills, troops, commonEvents)

data.description: Fields to set (or the complete record when merge=false)

merge.description: Merge into existing record (true) or replace (false)

tools.name: create_record
tools.description: Append a new record to a database. The new record's fields are copied from `data`; missing fields should be filled in to match the shape of existing records (fetch one with get_record as a template first). Returns the new id.

type.description: Which database to access (e.g. actors, items, skills, troops, commonEvents)

data.description: The record fields (id is assigned automatically)

tools.name: get_system
tools.description: Read System.json (game title, starting party/position, terms, sounds, switches, variables, etc.). Optionally return only one top-level key.

tools.name: set_switch_name
tools.description: Set the editor name of a game switch in System.json (e.g. switch 5 = 'Opened Chest'). The switches array grows if the id is beyond its current size.

tools.name: set_variable_name
tools.description: Set the editor name of a game variable in System.json (e.g. variable 3 = 'Quest Progress'). The variables array grows if the id is beyond its current size.

tools.name: update_system
tools.description: Shallow-merge the given top-level fields into System.json (e.g. gameTitle, startMapId, startX, startY, switches, variables).

tools.name: list_maps
tools.description: List all maps from MapInfos.json as {id, name, parentId, order}.

tools.name: get_map
tools.description: Read a map's properties (size, tileset, music, encounters, notes) and event summaries. Tile data is omitted unless includeTileData=true (it is large: width*height*6 integers).

tools.name: update_map
tools.description: Shallow-merge fields into a map's JSON (e.g. displayName, note, bgm, encounterList). Refuses to touch 'data' or 'events' — use the event tools for events and paint_tiles for tiles. To switch tilesets prefer set_map_tileset.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: Get the full JSON of one event on a map, including all pages and command lists.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Replace an event on a map with the given event JSON (same shape as returned by get_event). The event's id and its array position stay in sync automatically. See event_command_reference for command codes.

event.description: Complete event object (name, x, y, note, pages)

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Add a new event to a map at (x, y). If no pages are given, a single empty page (action-button trigger, no commands) is created. Returns the new event id.

pages.description: Optional event pages; defaults to one empty page

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete an event from a map. The slot is set to null so other event ids are unaffected (matches editor behavior).

tools.name: add_event_command
tools.description: Insert commands into an event page's command list without resending the whole event. Commands are inserted before the page's terminating {code: 0} entry (or at `index` if given). Multi-line constructs work naturally, e.g. Show Text is one code-101 command followed by code-401 commands. See event_command_reference for codes.

index.description: Position in the list to insert at; defaults to the end (before the terminator)

tools.name: add_dialogue
tools.description: Add spoken dialogue to an event page in one call — builds the Show Text (101) and text-line (401) commands automatically, splitting into multiple message boxes every 4 lines. Inserted before the page's end, like add_event_command.

lines.description: Dialogue lines (a new message box starts every 4 lines)

faceName.description: Face image file (e.g. 'Actor1'), empty for none

tools.name: create_map
tools.description: Create a new map: writes MapXXX.json and registers it in MapInfos.json. The map starts empty unless `fill` is given (a ground tile for layer 0); afterwards use paint_tiles to paint it, get_tileset_info to choose tiles and add events with the event tools. Returns the new map id.

parentId.description: Parent map id in the editor tree (0 = top level)

kind.description: Autotile kind, for sheets A1-A4 (A1 0-15, A2 16-47, A3 48-79, A4 80-127)

index.description: Tile index, for sheets A5 (0-127) and B-E (0-255)

fill.description: Optional tile to fill layer 0 with, e.g. {sheet:'A2', kind:16} for grass

tools.name: event_command_reference
tools.description: Reference table of RPG Maker MV event command codes and their parameters. Consult this before writing or editing event command lists.

tools.name: get_tileset_info
tools.description: Describe a tileset so you can choose tiles to paint: which image is assigned to each sheet (A1-A5, B-E), the tile id ranges, and for autotile sheets every kind with its type, position on the sheet image and passability. Without `sheet` you get an overview; pass `sheet` for the detail of one sheet (for A5/B-E that includes a passability grid laid out like the image: o passable, x blocked, * drawn above characters, p partly blocked). Use get_tileset_image to see what the tiles look like. `tileIds` decodes passability and terrain flags for specific tile ids.

tilesetId.description: Tileset id (a map's tilesetId, see get_map)

sheet.description: Return the detail of one sheet

tools.name: get_tileset_image
tools.description: Return one tileset sheet (A1-A5, B-E) as an image so you can see which tile looks like what, together with its grid layout (48px tiles). Use get_tileset_info for the matching tile ids and kinds.

tools.name: set_map_tileset
tools.description: Switch a map to another tileset (which sheets/tile images it uses). Existing tile ids are kept as they are, so they will show the new tileset's graphics - repaint with paint_tiles if the layouts differ.

tools.name: paint_tiles
tools.description: Paint tiles onto a map. Takes a list of operations applied in order: `cells` (individual positions), `rect` (filled or hollow rectangle) and `fill` (flood fill from a cell). Tiles are chosen as {sheet:'A2', kind:N} (autotile sheets A1-A4), {sheet:'B', index:N} (A5/B-E) or a raw tile id; 0 erases. Autotile edge, corner and wall shapes are calculated automatically, including re-shaping neighbours, just like painting in the editor. Layers: 0-1 ground, 2-3 upper tiles, 4 shadows, 5 regions. Typical map: fill layer 0 with a ground kind from A2, then place water/walls/objects on top. Use get_tileset_info / get_tileset_image to pick tiles and render_map to check the result.

kind.description: Autotile kind, for sheets A1-A4 (A1 0-15, A2 16-47, A3 48-79, A4 80-127)

index.description: Tile index, for sheets A5 (0-127) and B-E (0-255)

tile.description: Which tile to place. Either {sheet, kind} for autotile sheets A1-A4, {sheet, index} for A5/B/C/D/E, or a raw tile id (0 erases). Autotile edge shapes are computed automatically.

layer.description: Map layer: 0-1 ground tiles, 2-3 upper tiles, 4 shadow bits (0-15), 5 region id (0-255). Defaults to 0 for sheets A1-A5 and 2 for B-E; required when erasing.

hollow.description: Only paint the outline of the rectangle

tools.name: render_map
tools.description: Show a map's tiles as text so you can check what you painted. mode 'symbols' (default) draws one character per cell using the topmost tile of layers 0-3 (or only `layer`) with a legend naming each symbol; mode 'ids' prints raw tile ids of one layer. Use x/y/width/height to look at a region (default: up to 100x60 from the top-left).

tools.name: render_map_image
tools.description: Render a map to a PNG image so you can SEE what it looks like: all tile layers with correct autotile shapes, shadows and tiles that draw above characters, optionally the events' character sprites, coloured event markers with their ids, region ids, a tile grid and a passability overlay (red = blocked in at least one direction). This is the visual counterpart of render_map (text) - use it after paint_tiles / create_event / connect_maps to check your work. Marker colours: blue = event with a Transfer Player command (door/exit), orange = shows text, magenta = autorun/parallel, green = anything else. Needs the tileset images in img/tilesets (sheets without an image are drawn as flat colours and listed). Large maps are shrunk to fit ~1600px; pass x/y/width/height to zoom into a region and raise tileSize for detail.

width.description: Region width in tiles (default: to the map's right edge)

height.description: Region height in tiles (default: to the map's bottom edge)

tileSize.description: Pixels per map tile (48 = full resolution). Reduced automatically so the image stays under ~1600px

showEvents.description: Draw event character sprites, coloured id markers, both, or neither

showPassability.description: Tint blocked cells translucent red (blocked in at least one direction by the tileset flags)

tools.name: render_diff
tools.description: Show what changed on a map compared with an earlier version: a text summary (changed tile cells, added/removed/moved/edited events) plus a PNG of the CURRENT map with changed cells outlined yellow and added or moved events outlined green. By default it compares with the most recent backup session that contains the map (the state before this session's first edit); pass against.session to pick a session folder from list_backups, or against.changeset to compare with the pre-image of a committed changeset. Use it after bulk painting or generation to review exactly what you touched. If the map has no earlier version this session, it says so.

changeset.description: Changeset id; compares with its pre-edit copy of the map

against.description: Which earlier version to compare with (default: the most recent backup session containing this map)

tileSize.description: Pixels per map tile; reduced automatically so the image stays under ~1600px

tools.name: list_plugins
tools.description: List all plugins registered in js/plugins.js with status and parameters.

tools.name: configure_plugin
tools.description: Enable/disable a registered plugin and/or merge new values into its parameters (parameter values are always strings in RPG Maker MV).

name.description: Plugin name as it appears in list_plugins

parameters.description: Parameter values to merge into the plugin's parameters

tools.name: add_plugin
tools.description: Register an existing js/plugins/<name>.js file in the plugin list. Fails if the file does not exist (use create_plugin to make a new one).

tools.name: remove_plugin
tools.description: Remove a plugin from js/plugins.js. The plugin's .js file is NOT deleted.

tools.name: create_plugin
tools.description: Create a new plugin file in js/plugins/ and register it. If no code is given, a standard MV plugin scaffold (with @plugindesc header) is written. Fails if the file already exists.

code.description: Full JavaScript source; omit for a scaffold

tools.name: read_plugin
tools.description: Read the JavaScript source of js/plugins/<name>.js.

tools.name: write_plugin
tools.description: Overwrite the JavaScript source of an existing js/plugins/<name>.js.

tools.name: playtest_start
tools.description: Start a playtest of the current project. mode 'nwjs' launches the game with an NW.js runtime (pass runtimePath, e.g. the Game.exe inside the RPG Maker MV install's nwjs-win folder) and captures its stdout/stderr. mode 'browser' serves the project over a local HTTP server and returns a URL to open. Any previous playtest is stopped first.

runtimePath.description: Path to NW.js executable. If omitted in nwjs mode, common install locations (Steam, KADOKAWA, the project's own Game.exe, $RPGMAKER_MV_NWJS) are probed automatically.

tools.name: playtest_status
tools.description: Whether a playtest is running, in which mode, and its URL/PID.

tools.name: playtest_log
tools.description: Recent stdout/stderr lines from an NW.js playtest process.

tail.description: Number of lines from the end

tools.name: playtest_stop
tools.description: Stop the running playtest process and/or HTTP server.

tools.name: create_damage_skill
tools.description: Create a complete damaging skill in one call. The formula uses MV damage syntax where `a` is the user and `b` the target, e.g. 'a.mat * 4 - b.mdf * 2' or 'a.atk * 2 - b.def'. Returns the new skill id.

animationId.description: Animation id from the Animations database (0 = none, -1 = normal attack)

stypeId.description: Skill type id (1 = Magic by default)

occasion.description: When usable: 0 always, 1 battle only, 2 menu only, 3 never

damageType.description: What the damage hits (drain variants absorb into the user)

elementId.description: Element id from System types (0 = none, -1 = normal attack element)

scope.description: Target scope: 1 one enemy, 2 all enemies, 3-6 random enemies (1-4), 7 one ally, 8 all allies, 9 one dead ally, 10 all dead allies, 11 the user

tpGain.description: TP the user gains on use

tools.name: create_healing_skill
tools.description: Create a complete healing skill in one call. The formula uses MV damage syntax (`a` = user), e.g. 'a.mat * 2 + 200'. Heals HP or MP; optionally also removes states (e.g. a cure spell).

animationId.description: Animation id from the Animations database (0 = none, -1 = normal attack)

stypeId.description: Skill type id (1 = Magic by default)

occasion.description: When usable: 0 always, 1 battle only, 2 menu only, 3 never

scope.description: Target scope: 1 one enemy, 2 all enemies, 3-6 random enemies (1-4), 7 one ally, 8 all allies, 9 one dead ally, 10 all dead allies, 11 the user (default: one ally)

removeStates.description: State ids to remove from the target (100% chance), e.g. poison

tools.name: create_buff_skill
tools.description: Create a skill that applies parameter buffs and/or debuffs. Parameter ids: 0 Max HP, 1 Max MP, 2 Attack, 3 Defense, 4 M.Attack, 5 M.Defense, 6 Agility, 7 Luck. If only debuffs are given the scope defaults to one enemy, otherwise one ally.

animationId.description: Animation id from the Animations database (0 = none, -1 = normal attack)

stypeId.description: Skill type id (1 = Magic by default)

occasion.description: When usable: 0 always, 1 battle only, 2 menu only, 3 never

buffs.description: Buffs to add to the target

debuffs.description: Debuffs to add to the target

scope.description: Target scope: 1 one enemy, 2 all enemies, 3-6 random enemies (1-4), 7 one ally, 8 all allies, 9 one dead ally, 10 all dead allies, 11 the user

tools.name: create_state_skill
tools.description: Create a skill that adds or removes states (poison, sleep, etc.) on the target, each with its own success chance. State ids come from the States database (list_records type=states).

animationId.description: Animation id from the Animations database (0 = none, -1 = normal attack)

stypeId.description: Skill type id (1 = Magic by default)

occasion.description: When usable: 0 always, 1 battle only, 2 menu only, 3 never

scope.description: Target scope: 1 one enemy, 2 all enemies, 3-6 random enemies (1-4), 7 one ally, 8 all allies, 9 one dead ally, 10 all dead allies, 11 the user (default: one enemy for add, one ally for remove)

tools.name: search_records
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search across database records (name, nickname, description, note, profile, messages). Searches one type, or all types when type is omitted. Returns {type, id, name, matchedIn} summaries.

type.description: Database to search; omit to search all databases

tools.name: search_map_events
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search across events on one map or every map. Matches event names and notes; with searchCommands=true it also searches inside event command parameters (message text, script lines, plugin commands). Returns {mapId, mapName, eventId, name, x, y, matchedIn}.

mapId.description: Search only this map; omit for all maps

searchCommands.description: Also search inside event command lists (slower, finds text/script content)

tools.name: list_backups
tools.description: List automatic backup sessions in <project>/.mcp-backups. A file is snapshotted there the first time each server session modifies it, so every session can be rolled back with restore_backup.

tools.name: restore_backup
tools.description: Restore project files from a backup session (see list_backups). Restores one file (project-relative path like 'data/Actors.json') or, with no file given, every file in the session. The current state is itself backed up first, so a restore can be undone. Refused while a changeset is open (commit or discard it first). The RPG Maker editor must stay closed while files are restored.

session.description: Backup session name from list_backups; defaults to the most recent

file.description: Project-relative file to restore; omit to restore all files in the session

tools.name: editor_status
tools.description: Check whether the RPG Maker MV editor appears to be running and which files this server wrote have since been changed by something else (usually the editor saving over them). Report only: it never blocks or undoes any edit.

tools.name: validate_project
tools.description: Integrity check of the whole project: parses every database file, verifies MapInfos entries have map files (and finds orphaned map files), checks registered plugins have source files, and scans event commands for references to missing common events or transfer destinations. Returns errors (broken) and warnings (suspicious).

tools.name: begin_changeset
tools.description: Start a transactional batch of edits. While a changeset is open, every edit tool stages its result in memory: nothing is written to disk until commit_changeset, and all reads (get_map, get_record, list_plugins, ...) reflect the staged edits. Commit writes every staged file in one step (all or nothing) and can be rolled back later with undo_changeset; discard_changeset drops the staged edits. Only one changeset can be open at a time; restore_backup is refused while one is open and set_project discards it. Playtests read from disk, so they only see committed edits. The RPG Maker editor must stay closed while the server edits the project.

label.description: Short description of the batch, e.g. 'Add the blacksmith to Town'

tools.name: commit_changeset
tools.description: Write every file staged by the open changeset to disk as one unit and return a per-file summary (created/modified, event/tile/record counts). Staged .json files are validated first: if any is invalid, nothing is written and the changeset stays open. Pre-images are journaled under .mcp-backups/changesets/<id>/ so undo_changeset can roll the commit back; a commit interrupted by a crash is rolled back automatically the next time the project is opened (the files found on disk are backed up first). Other edits are refused while the commit runs. If a commit fails and its files cannot all be restored, the changeset is closed and every edit is refused until undo_changeset has restored them. Until this is called, nothing of the changeset is on disk and reads reflect the staged edits. The RPG Maker editor must stay closed while the server edits the project.

tools.name: discard_changeset
tools.description: Drop every edit staged by the open changeset. Nothing on disk changes (nothing of the changeset was on disk yet), and reads go back to the files on disk. The RPG Maker editor must stay closed while the server edits the project.

tools.name: undo_changeset
tools.description: Roll back the most recently committed changeset from its journal: modified files are restored byte-for-byte, files it created are deleted. Call repeatedly to step back through earlier commits. Edits made to those files after the commit are overwritten too. Refused while a changeset is open (while one is open, reads reflect its staged edits and nothing is on disk until commit). The RPG Maker editor must stay closed while the server edits the project.

tools.name: connect_maps
tools.description: Link two maps with Transfer Player events in both directions in one call. A door event is placed on each map; stepping on (or pressing OK at) the door on map A moves the player to map B's spawn tile and vice versa. Give each side its `door` tile; add `spawn` when the player should appear next to the door instead of on it (always do this for doors drawn into walls). Both maps are validated before anything is written, and a door is refused if another event already stands on that tile (allowOverlap overrides). Use twoWay=false for a one-way link (map A's door only). Check the result with render_map_image (doors show as blue markers) and list_map_connections.

door.description: Tile where this map's exit event is placed

direction.description: Facing on arrival: 0 keep, 2 down, 4 left, 6 right, 8 up

spawn.description: Where the player appears when they ARRIVE on this map through the connection. Defaults to the door tile - give a spawn tile in front of the door when the door is in a wall.

twoWay.description: Create the return door on map B as well

trigger.description: touch = player walks onto the door tile, action = player presses OK facing it

doorName.description: Event name prefix; default 'To <destination map name>'

sound.description: Sound effect to play before leaving, e.g. {name: 'Open1'}

tools.name: list_map_connections
tools.description: Scan every map's events for Transfer Player commands and show how the maps are linked: each door with its destination, one-way links without a way back, transfers to maps that do not exist, and maps that cannot be reached from the game's start map. Transfers whose target is chosen by variables are listed as dynamic and cannot be followed, so 'unreachable' is a hint, not proof.

mapId.description: Only list doors on this map (the reachability analysis still uses all maps)

tools.name: bulk_update_records
tools.description: Change one or more fields on many database records at once, with a diff. Example - all weapons +10% attack: {type: 'weapons', changes: [{field: 'params.atk', op: 'percent', value: 10}]}. Select records with `ids` and/or `where` conditions (all must match); with neither, every record is selected. Fields are paths such as 'price', 'params.atk' (mhp/mmp/atk/def/mat/mdf/agi/luk), 'params[2]', 'damage.formula', 'traits[0].value'. Ops: set (any value), add, multiply, percent (+value%) - numeric ops round to whole numbers for integer fields (round: auto), with optional min/max clamps. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: nothing is written until you pass dryRun=false, so show the diff to the user first. If any record fails, nothing is written.

where.description: Conditions, e.g. [{field: 'wtypeId', op: 'eq', value: 1}, {field: 'name', op: 'contains', value: 'sword'}]

dryRun.description: true = only preview the diff (default), false = write the changes

maxPreview.description: Maximum records shown in the diff

tools.name: generate_param_curve
tools.description: Generate stat curves over levels and (optionally) write them into a class. Each curve goes from `start` at minLevel to `end` at maxLevel with a shape: linear, ease-in (slow start), ease-out (fast start), ease-in-out, exponential (constant growth factor) or logistic (S-curve). Without classId this is a pure preview of the numbers. With classId the class's params table is rewritten for minLevel..maxLevel (other levels are untouched) - dry run by default, pass dryRun=false to apply. Follow up with balance_report to see how the new curve plays against enemies.

start.description: Value at the first point of the curve

exponent.description: Power for ease shapes (default 2), steepness for logistic (default 8)

param.description: mhp, mmp, atk, def, mat, mdf, agi, luk (or 0-7)

classId.description: Write the curves into this class

tools.name: generate_enemy_scaling
tools.description: Spread enemy stats along a curve for smooth difficulty progression. Give the enemies ordered from weakest to strongest; the first gets each curve's `start`, the last its `end`, the rest are interpolated with the chosen shape. Curves can target any parameter (mhp, mmp, atk, def, mat, mdf, agi, luk) plus `exp` and `gold`. Dry run by default - shows before and after per enemy; pass dryRun=false to write.

enemyIds.description: Enemy ids from weakest to strongest

start.description: Value at the first point of the curve

exponent.description: Power for ease shapes (default 2), steepness for logistic (default 8)

tools.name: balance_report
tools.description: Measure the game's balance from its data: (1) class stat curves at chosen levels, (2) the attack skill's damage by level against a reference enemy, (3) a matrix of attackers vs enemies (average damage and hits to kill) and (4) enemy threat vs the same characters (damage of the enemy's best attack and hits to kill them). Ends with warnings: unevaluable damage formulas, curves that go down, enemies killed in one hit or immune, enemies that one-shot a character. Attackers default to the starting party. Numbers are averages with no variance, crits or misses and ignore states, items and elements beyond what the skill/traits specify - use simulate_battle for a full fight.

classIds.description: Classes for the curve tables (default: the first 6)

attackers.description: Characters for the matrices; default: the starting party at their initial level

referenceEnemyId.description: Enemy for the damage-by-level table (default: the one with median HP)

tools.name: simulate_battle
tools.description: Run many simulated battles of a troop against a party and report win rate, turns, how much HP the party keeps and who does the damage or dies. Uses the project's real stats (class curves, equipment, traits), damage formulas, variance, critical hits, hit/evasion rates, agility turn order, target weighting (TGR) and enemy action ratings. Party members use `skillIds` in order (first affordable one, healing only when an ally is below 60% HP), falling back to the Attack skill. Not modelled: states, buffs, items, guarding, TP, enemy conditions on states/switches (treated as false). Seeded, so results are reproducible. Default party: the starting party at their initial level.

level.description: Set every party member to this level

tools.name: export_texts
tools.description: Export every translatable text of the project to a CSV or JSON file inside the project (default localization/texts.csv) with columns key, context, original, translation. Covers database names/descriptions/messages, System terms and type names, the game title, map display names, and event text (dialogue boxes as one row each with lines joined by newlines, choices, scrolling text, actor name/nickname/profile commands) in maps, common events and troop battle events. If the file already exists its translations are carried over by key, so re-exporting after changes never loses work. Fill in the translation column (leave empty to keep the original), then use import_texts. See the rpgmaker-localization skill for rules about control codes and message length.

file.description: Output path relative to the project folder (default localization/texts.<format>)

tools.name: import_texts
tools.description: Apply the translation column of a file written by export_texts back into the project's data. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: reports what would change and nothing is written until dryRun=false. Rows with an empty translation are skipped. A row whose `original` no longer matches the project text (the text changed after export) is skipped unless force=true. Dialogue translations longer than 4 lines are split into several message boxes automatically; choices are kept in sync. Control codes (\C[n], \V[n], \N[n] ...) are compared with the original and mismatches are reported as warnings.

file.description: Path relative to the project folder, e.g. localization/texts.csv

force.description: Apply rows even if their original text no longer matches

tools.name: audit_assets
tools.description: Checks that every image and audio file the project references exists on disk, and optionally lists files nothing references. Scanned references: Actors (characterName, faceName, battlerName); Enemies battlerName (img/enemies, or img/sv_enemies when System optSideView is on); Tilesets tilesetNames; Maps (parallaxName, bgm, bgs, battleback1Name, battleback2Name, event page images); event commands 101 (face), 231 (picture), 241/245/249/250 (BGM/BGS/ME/SE) and 322 (actor graphics) in map events, common events and troops; System (title1Name, title2Name, battleback1Name, battleback2Name, titleBgm, battleBgm, victoryMe, defeatMe, gameoverMe, boat/ship/airship bgm, sounds). Anything else is listed under notScanned, so 'unused' can include files used only by plugins or scripts. Audio is satisfied by either an .ogg or an .m4a file. caseMismatch means the file exists only with different letter case: it works on Windows but breaks on Linux, macOS and web deployments. Each list is capped at 200 entries; truncated gives the omitted counts.

includeUnused.description: Also list asset files that no scanned reference uses.

tools.name: lint_events
tools.description: Statically checks event command lists in map events, common events and troop pages. Rules: unterminated-list and block-structure (missing code 0 terminator, unclosed or mismatched choices/branches/loops, indent jumps; error), unreachable-command (a command right after Exit Event Processing at the same indent; warning), long-message-line (a Show Text line too long for the window; warning), transfer-missing-map and transfer-out-of-bounds (direct Transfer Player to a map not in MapInfos or outside its size; error), missing-common-event (Common Event call to an id that does not exist; error), unnamed-switch and unnamed-variable (Control Switches/Variables on ids with no name in System.json; info). Variable-designated transfers are not checked. long-message-line removes message control codes (\C[n], \V[n], \N[n], \P[n], \I[n], \{ \} \. \| \! \> \< \^) and compares the remaining character count with maxLineChars; the default of 50 is only an approximation, since real fit depends on the font, face graphic and window width. Findings carry location {kind, mapId, eventId, page, index}; page and index are 0-based positions in the event's pages and command list (common events use page 0, troops use the troop id as eventId). minSeverity defaults to warning, so info findings appear only when requested. scope defaults to all; mapId limits the map part to one map. Maps whose file cannot be read are listed in skippedMaps. Results are sorted by severity then location and capped at 300 findings; counts cover all findings and truncated is the number cut.

mapId.description: Lint only this map (affects the maps part of the scope).

maxLineChars.description: Longest allowed Show Text line after control codes are removed (approximate).

tools.name: simulate_event
tools.description: Dry-runs one map event page against a hypothetical game state and returns what it would do, without touching the project or running the game. Supported commands: Show Text (101/401), Show Choices (102/402/403/404), Conditional Branch (111/411/412: switch, variable, self switch, gold, item), Loop/Break (112/113/413), Exit Event Processing (115), Common Event (117, nested up to 8 deep), comments, Control Switches (121), Control Variables (122: constant, variable and random operands), Control Self Switch (123), Change Gold (125), Change Items (126), Transfer Player (201, ends the run) and Plugin Command (356, listed in changes as 'plugin: ...'). Everything else (script 355, audio, pictures, movement, waits, labels, other condition types, game-data operands) is listed in unsupported with its index and skipped; an unsupported condition follows unknownCondition: stop (default) ends the run with ended 'unsupported', then/else takes that branch. Message text is returned verbatim, control codes unexpanded. Limits: 10000 steps (ended 'stepLimit'), integer variable math (results are floored like the engine, so -7 / 2 gives -4; division or modulo by zero leaves the variable unchanged; a random or variable operand is evaluated once per command). A command that changes several switches or variables adds one changes entry for the whole range. messages, changes and unsupported are each capped at 2000 entries; omitted counts what was dropped (present only then) and finalState stays exact. State inputs default to everything OFF/0/empty: switches and variables are keyed by id, selfSwitches by letter A to D, items by item id. choices lists the answers to Show Choices in the order they are asked (0-based; a missing answer is 0, an out-of-range one takes the cancel branch). page is a 0-based page index; when omitted the highest page whose conditions hold under the supplied state is used (the actor condition counts as met). The random operand is seeded (default seed 0), so runs repeat exactly. Returns {messages, changes, transfers, unsupported, ended, finalState, pageUsed}.

page.description: 0-based page index; omit to pick the page that would be active under the supplied state.

switches.description: Switch states by id, e.g. {"12": true}.

selfSwitches.description: Self switches of this event, e.g. {"A": true}.

choices.description: Answers to Show Choices, in the order they are asked.

unknownCondition.description: What to do at a condition that cannot be simulated.

tools.name: build_dialogue_tree
tools.description: Compiles a nested dialogue tree into correctly indented event commands (messages, choices, conditions, switches, variables, transfers) and optionally inserts it into an event page, so you never hand-write indents or block terminators. With mapId + eventId the commands are inserted at indent 0 before the page's end (or at `index`), like add_event_command; without them, or with dryRun, nothing is written and the compiled commands are returned in `preview`. `tree` is an array of nodes, nested at most 8 levels deep. Node vocabulary: {say: string | string[], face?: {name, index}, background?: 0|1|2, position?: 0|1|2} (4 lines per message box; "\n" splits lines; control codes like \C[2] are kept as written); {choices: [{label, then?: Node[]}] (1-6), cancel?: "disallow" (default) | "branch" | choiceIndex}; {if: Condition, then?: Node[], else?: Node[]} with Condition = {switch, is?} | {variable, op: "eq"|"ne"|"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte", value} | {selfSwitch: "A".."D", is?} | {gold} (party has at least) | {item} (party has item); {setSwitch: {id, value}} | {setVariable: {id, op: "set"|"add"|"sub", value}} | {setSelfSwitch: {ch, value}} | {transfer: {mapId, x, y, direction?: 0|2|4|6|8, fade?: 0|1|2}} | {raw: [{code, indent?, parameters?}]} (indent is relative to the node's position). Example: [{"say":"Will you help?","face":{"name":"Actor1","index":0}},{"choices":[{"label":"Yes","then":[{"setSwitch":{"id":5,"value":true}},{"say":"Thank you!"}]},{"label":"No","then":[{"say":"A pity."}]}],"cancel":"branch"}]. Returns { commands, inserted?, problems, preview? }; preview is included for dry runs and for trees of up to 40 commands.

mapId.description: Map to insert into; omit (with eventId) for a dry run

eventId.description: Event to insert into; omit (with mapId) for a dry run

index.description: Position in the page's command list to insert at; defaults to the end (before the terminator). Positions inside a conditional or choice body, or on a continuation line of a multi-line command (text, comment, script or shop lines: 401, 405, 408, 605, 655), are refused

dryRun.description: Compile and validate only; never touches the project files

tools.name: create_event_from_template
tools.description: Creates a complete, ready-to-use map event at (x, y) from a template, in one write. Refuses out-of-bounds tiles, and refuses a tile that already holds an event unless allowStack is true. Graphics default to none: events are INVISIBLE in game until an image is supplied (chest: closedImage/openImage, npc: image; locked_door, inn, shop and save_point never get a graphic and are meant to sit on a tile that already looks right). Templates and their params: chest {reward: {gold?, item?: {type: item|weapon|armor, id, count?}}, message?, closedImage?, openImage?} (two pages: the action button opens it and sets self switch A, then an empty opened page; if only closedImage is given, openImage defaults to the same graphic with direction 8 - the opened-chest frame of the standard chest sheets); locked_door {keyItemId, destination: {mapId, x, y, direction?: 0|2|4|6|8}, lockedMessage?, consumeKey?} (transfers the player if the party holds the key); inn {price, greeting?} (Stay/Leave choice; staying charges gold, fades out, restores the party, fades in); shop {goods: [{type: item|weapon|armor, id, price?}] (1-40; price defaults to the database price), purchaseOnly?}; save_point {} (opens the save screen); npc {lines: string[], face?: {name, index}, image?}. Image = {characterName, characterIndex (0-7), direction?: 2|4|6|8, pattern?: 0|1|2}. Returns { eventId, name, pages }.

name.description: Event name; defaults to the template name (Chest, Door, Inn, Shop, Save Point, NPC)

allowStack.description: Allow placing the event on a tile that already has an event

template.description: Which template to build; the other fields depend on it

reward.description: chest: { gold?: number, item?: {type: item|weapon|armor, id, count?} }, at least one

message.description: chest: text shown when opened (default "You found treasure!")

characterName.description: Character sheet name in img/characters, e.g. "People1" or "!Chest"

characterIndex.description: Which of the 8 characters on the sheet (0-7)

openImage.description: chest: graphic after opening (default: closedImage facing up)

keyItemId.description: locked_door: item id of the key

lockedMessage.description: locked_door: text when the player has no key (default "It's locked.")

consumeKey.description: locked_door: remove one key on use

goods.description: shop: 1-40 entries { type: item|weapon|armor, id, price? }; omit price for the database price

lines.description: npc: lines of dialogue (4 per message box)

tools.name: generate_map
tools.description: Procedurally generate a dungeon (rooms joined by corridors) or a cave (organic, one connected region) and paint it with a tile profile. Give exactly one of `mapId` (generate into an existing map, using its size and tileset) or `create` (make a new map and register it in MapInfos.json). An existing map that has any tile or any event is refused unless `overwrite` is true; overwrite resets every tile layer and removes all events. `seed` makes the result repeatable; when omitted a random seed is picked, and the seed used is always returned. The profile (floor, wall, optional wallTop, optional weighted decor) defaults to suggestTileProfile, which works from the tileset's data only: the lowest-numbered walkable A2 kind as floor (else the first walkable A5 tile), the lowest-numbered blocking A4 wall kind as wall with the floor-rule A4 kind above it as wall top (else the first blocking A5 or B tile), and no decor. The profile used and the reasoning are returned as profileUsed and profileNotes. Nothing is written when the profile's floor is not walkable, its wall or wall top does not block movement, a sheet has no image, or the painted map is not fully reachable from the entrance. Markers are empty placeholder events at priority 0 (below characters, so they never block the player) named Entrance, Exit and Chest 1..n, placed on floor cells; chests are random floor cells away from the entrance and exit, chosen so that no chest cuts off any part of the map. `markers` defaults to {entrance: true, exit: true, chests: 0}. The result lists each marker's eventId and position under `markers`. Afterwards: call render_map_image to look at the result (consider showPassability); wire doors to other maps with connect_maps using the returned entrance and exit coordinates; fill the chest markers with create_event_from_template or the event tools. A marker occupies its tile: delete it with delete_event before placing a door or chest there, or pass allowOverlap (connect_maps) / allowStack (create_event_from_template) to place on top of it. A dungeon needs a map of at least 14x7 (or 7x14) cells; smaller maps are refused with a clear error (caves are reliable from about 13x13, and MV's default 17x13 never failed in testing; 9x9 to 12x12 and thin maps fail for many seeds, so try another seed or a larger map). Limits: decor is best-effort (sparse, only on open floor), and wall faces are a one-row simplification, since many tilesets draw wall sides two or more tiles tall.

mapId.description: Existing map to generate into (use instead of `create`)

parentId.description: Parent map id in the editor tree (0 = top level)

create.description: New map to create (use instead of `mapId`)

seed.description: Same seed, size and options give the same layout; random when omitted

kind.description: Autotile kind, for sheets A1-A4 (A1 0-15, A2 16-47, A3 48-79, A4 80-127)

index.description: Tile index, for sheets A5 (0-127) and B-E (0-255)

wall.description: Tile for wall cells (should be impassable)

wallTop.description: Optional tile for the top of walls, e.g. an A4 wall-top kind

decor.description: Optional decoration tiles scattered on the floor, picked in proportion to their weight

profile.description: Tiles to paint with; defaults to a suggestion from the tileset

overwrite.description: Allow replacing a map that already has tiles or events

tools.name: capture_stamp
tools.description: Save a rectangle of a map as a reusable stamp in <project>/.mcp-stamps/<name>.json: all six layers (tiles, shadow bits, regions) and, with includeEvents (default true), the events standing inside it. Use place_stamp to paste it onto any map of the same tileset. Width and height are 1-64 and the whole rectangle must lie inside the map. Names are 1-64 characters (letters, digits, space, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit). An existing stamp is only replaced when overwrite is true. Stamps are written like any project file, so inside an open changeset they are only staged until commit_changeset. Add .mcp-stamps/ to .gitignore next to .mcp-backups/ unless you want to share stamps.

includeEvents.description: Also capture the events inside the rectangle

overwrite.description: Replace a stamp that already has this name

tools.name: place_stamp
tools.description: Paste a stamp made with capture_stamp onto a map with its top-left corner at (x, y). The whole stamp must fit inside the map (it is never clipped) and the map must use the same tileset the stamp was captured from. The rectangle is REPLACED on every layer: empty stamp cells erase what was there. Autotile cells (A1-A4) are re-shaped so their edges blend with the surroundings, including the cells next to the stamp; all other tiles, shadow bits and regions are copied as they are. With includeEvents (default true) the stamp's events are added with new ids and moved to the placement; if one would land on a cell that already has an event, nothing is placed and the cells are listed (includeEvents: false places only the tiles). There is no rotate or mirror. A backup of the map is kept.

tools.name: list_stamps
tools.description: List the stamps saved in <project>/.mcp-stamps/ (name, size, tilesetId, event count), sorted by name. Stamps captured inside a changeset that is still open are not listed until it is committed.

tools.name: install_skills
tools.description: Copy the bundled RPG Maker skill files (workflow guides for map building, event writing, balancing, localization, plugins) into the project's .claude/skills folder so Claude Code picks them up automatically in that project. The same files are always available as resources (rpgmaker://skills/<name>). Existing skill folders are skipped unless overwrite=true.

overwrite.description: Replace skill files that already exist
